hypothesis: Per the ESMM literature note (Ma et al. 2018) already retrieved for this project, add `is_like` as an auxiliary pointwise-BCE training signal sharing the FM's embedding table `V` with the main long_view BPR task (separate small linear heads `W_main`/`W_aux` per task, main task still scored/evaluated alone). This gives the shared embeddings a second, denser (though still sparse) supervision source every epoch, which should act as a regularizer on `V` and reduce the overfitting pattern that has plagued every long_view-only FM variant tried so far, without adding raw score-function capacity (unlike the rejected DeepFM attempt).
reflection: The DeepFM+dropout swap (iter 7) still overfit after its epoch-2 peak despite dropout regularization — more raw interaction capacity alone didn't fix the underlying signal-scarcity problem, since it's still trained on `long_view` alone. Given the plateau, I have a specific reason to skip the research question this turn: the literature already retrieved (ESMM, SIGIR 2018) directly names the exact untried mechanism worth trying — jointly modeling `long_view` with a denser auxiliary signal (`is_like`) via a shared embedding table — and I have a concrete, implementable plan for it without needing more external search.
expected_effect: GAUC should move more than nDCG@5, since the auxiliary task densifies gradient signal across the whole training set (not just top-of-list discrimination), which should primarily improve global embedding calibration/generalization rather than fine top-5 ordering.
